issues.failure_explanation: The displayed implication allows arbitrary (unconstrained-sign) multipliers on inactive constraints: it hypothesizes the joint-gradient equation with the full sum over all i=1..m and sign conditions only on I(x,θ). Counterexample: n=q=1, p=m=1, H(x,θ)=x+θ, g₁(x,θ)=−x−θ−1; at (0,0) the point is feasible and MFCQ holds (∇_x h=1, I=∅). With (λ,μ)=(1,1): λ∇g₁+J_xH^Tμ = −(1,1)+(1,1)=0 (joint gradients) and the sign condition is vacuous, but μ=1≠0. The correct dual characterization of the joint MFCQ sums only over i∈I(x,θ), as in eq:22122025b.

failure_location.quote: If the MFCQ is satisfied at \((\pvar, \param)\), then the following holds for the joint Jacobians in \(\pvar,\param\), \begin{align}\label{eq:mfcqduo}       &\transp{\jac\!G(\pvar, \param)}\dvar + \transp{\jac\!H(\pvar, \param)}\dvarr = 0, \text{ and } \dvar_i \geq 0, \forall\, i \in  I(\pvar, \param) \nonumber \\\     &\implies \dvarr = 0, \dvar_i = 0, \forall\, i \in  I(\pvar, \param).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the sum in eq:mfcqduo to i ∈ I(x,θ) (mirroring eq:22122025b), or restate the remark using only the primal joint MFCQ (valid since the MFCQ direction d_x can be taken with d_θ=0).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed 'equivalent dual formulation' of the joint MFCQ in Remark rem:jointMFCQ is false. The verbal conclusion (the joint MFCQ holds) is true in primal form, and the later Section 4.2 use only needs the true primal statement, so no downstream formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Dual joint-MFCQ characterization in Remark rem:jointMFCQ is false
issues.why_classification: One-line correction of the displayed formula; the joint MFCQ itself (needed downstream) holds via its primal form, so no substantive claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Taking the limit in {\eqref{eq:22122025a}}, we can write\n    \begin{equation}\label{eq:21122025a}\n        \transp{\jac_{\pvar}\!G(\pvar, \param)}\alpha + \transp{\jac_{\pvar}\!H(\pvar, \param)}\beta = 0.

issues.failure_explanation: From stationarity one only gets J_xG(x_k,θ_k)^Tα_k + J_xH(x_k,θ_k)^Tβ_k = −v_k/‖(λ_k,μ_k)‖ with ‖(λ_k,μ_k)‖ → ∞. Equation eq:22122025a instead divides by ‖(α_k,β_k)‖ = 1, so its right-hand side tends to −v ≠ 0 in general, and the limit equation eq:21122025a (right-hand side 0) does not follow. The contradiction with the dual MFCQ in eq:22122025b is therefore not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:22122025a by J_xG(x_k,θ_k)^Tα_k + J_xH(x_k,θ_k)^Tβ_k = −v_k/‖(λ_k,μ_k)‖ (dividing the stationarity relation by ‖(λ_k,μ_k)‖ → ∞); boundedness of (v_k) then gives the limit equation eq:21122025a, and the rest of the proof stands unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The written proof of local boundedness (and nonemptiness) of sol_pd fails; the conclusion itself is true and survives a one-line repair, so Theorem theo:main, which invokes Proposition prop:locboundp only through its conclusion, is not invalidated.
issues.title: Invalid normalization step in the proof of Proposition prop:locboundp
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the normalization (divide by ‖(λ_k,μ_k)‖ instead of ‖(α_k,β_k)‖ = 1) restores the argument verbatim; no mathematical content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem defines D_f(θ) with the convex hull conv D_F, but the proof's density step asserts D_f(θ(t)) = {u : ∃y ∈ solpd(θ(t)), (0,u) ∈ D_ℒ(y,θ(t))} where D_ℒ was defined as D_F + jacobians without convexification, and then applies the Castaing/density argument (Lemmas lem:edlem8, lem:edlem9) to the selections of the unconvexified D_ℒ. The displayed equality is false in general (D_F need not be convex-valued), so the chain rule is established only for u in the closure of the per-selection slices, a subset that may be proper in D_f(θ(t)); the chain rule for all u ∈ D_f(θ(t)) is not obtained as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Convexify in the density step: apply Lemma lem:edlem8 to the convexified definable compact-valued map t ↦ conv D_ℒ(y(t),θ(t)) (or, equivalently, note that the chain rule extends from the dense definable selections to all finite convex combinations, the a.e. full-measure set being uniform and the pairing linear), and keep the equality with lem:edlem9's convexified right-hand side.
issues.overall_effect: The central conservative-field statement of Theorem theo:main (and hence Theorem theo:mainsmooth, its smooth special case, and the conservative-field consequences advertised in rem:consequenceasm) is unsupported by the written proof, although the statement itself is true.
issues.title: Convex hull dropped in the density step of the proof of Theorem theo:main
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, contained argument (convexification of the selections and linearity of the pairing) that preserves the theorem exactly; no new global proof architecture or weakening of the advertised guarantee is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any \(k \in \N\), consider \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k)\) such that \(r_k > 0\), \(r_k \xrightarrow[k \to \infny]{} 0\), and \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k) \cap \Bcal(z_{s},r_{s}) = \varnothing\) for \(s \neq k\). Such a choice is possible, because for each $k$, $z_k$ is at positive distance of \(z_i\) for each $i \neq k$ and at positive distance of \(C\) the set of accumulation points.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiability (and local Lipschitz continuity) of the bump sum ḡ = f̄ + Σ_k φ(‖z−z_k‖/r_k)r_k is asserted with no argument, and it is false for admissible radii: the construction only requires r_k > 0, r_k → 0 and pairwise disjoint balls (with r_k ≤ dist(z_k,C) implicitly needed for ḡ|_C = 0). Taking, e.g., C = [0,1]×{0} and radii r_k comparable to dist(z_k,C) (e.g. r_k = dist(z_k,C)/3, admissible when the bumps are separated), at a point z̄ ∈ C approached by bump centers with z_k = (t_k, h_k), h_k ≫ |t_k − z̄|, one has ḡ(z_k) ≥ φ(0)r_k while ‖z_k − z̄‖ ~ dist(z_k,C) ~ r_k, so the difference quotient stays bounded away from 0 while ḡ ≡ 0 along C; hence ḡ is not differentiable at z̄. The claimed properties are therefore unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: Then, \(\bar{g}(z)= 0\) for every \(z \in C\), and \(\bar{g}(z) > 0\) for every \(z \in \Rell \setminus C\). Moreover  \(\bar{g}\) is differentiable and locally Lipschitz on \(\Rell\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose r_k ≤ dist(z_k,C)^2 (while keeping the balls pairwise disjoint) and verify the flatness ḡ(z) = o(dist(z,C)) at every point of C (bump k contributes O(r_k) = O(dist(z,C)²) on B_k, and points of B_k are at distance ≥ dist(z_k,C) − r_k from C), together with the bounded-gradient (hence local Lipschitz) argument; the stated conclusions then all hold.
issues.overall_effect: Claim lem:fnctcounterex (existence of a differentiable, locally Lipschitz, path differentiable C¹-off-C function with B_c(0,1) ⊂ ∂^cḡ on C) is not established as written, and the counterexample Claim theo:counterex built on it loses its support.
issues.title: Differentiability of the counterexample function asserted without the needed control on bump radii
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained but genuinely nontrivial argument (a suitable decay condition on the radii plus a flatness estimate at C-points); it preserves every substantive claim, so it is more than minor but not a loss of any result.
